title: Honest Interval Length for Squared Counterfactual-Density Effects near Equality under Known Design
banked_reason: Sound lower envelope and honest stratified bracket fall below the field floor; the promised rough-regime sharp simultaneous frontier and critical calibration remain open.
gap_reasons: The promised rough-regime sharp, simultaneously attaining honest-length frontier is still an open-ended question: the core delivers a lower envelope and an explicit nonmatching bracket, not the named explicit rate and data-only attaining interval required by the kernel (and the coupled critical calibration remains deferred).

Position this proved bracket at theorem level as a known-design/full-class-honest partial-frontier result and compare it precisely with the closest cited honest-inference and density-effect results; the current theorem lacks its own novelty, significance, and closest-result comparison.

FawkesHuEvansSejdinovic2022Matched appears in the bibliography but has no relevance sentence in related_work or the comparator table; add its precise relationship to this calibration question or remove the unused citation.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived a sound lower envelope and observable full-class honest stratified bracket, solving exact equality for beta>s/(4s+1) and the all-radius frontier for beta>1/4. The rough simultaneous frontier remains nonmatching (at beta=1/10,s=1,r=0, n^(-16/29) versus (log n/n)^(2/5)), and critical calibration is unproved. D0.5 math passed but the decision referee required revision and the general referee graded incremental below the field floor; no Lean formalization was attempted.
tldr: Squared marginal counterfactual-density effects distinguish distributional changes that mean effects miss, but their first derivative vanishes at marginal-density equality, \(p_{1,P}=p_{0,P}\). For full-class honest intervals, the proved lower envelope has equality elbow \(\beta_0(s)=2s/(8s+3)\); known-design stratification gives one observable interval and proves \(\mathcal J_n(0)\asymp D_n\) when \(\beta>s/(4s+1)\), and the complete simultaneous frontier \(\mathcal J_n(r)\asymp D_n+r/\sqrt n\) when \(\beta>1/4\). In rough regimes the proved lower and upper bounds need not coincide: the matching upper construction, intermediate-radius term, boundary logarithms, and feasible critical calibration remain open. The density envelope and separate coordinate regularity are prospective scientific benchmark restrictions. The priority claim concerns full-class local honest length, not counterfactual-density minimax theory announced in 2023.
gap: Kennedy, Balakrishnan and Wasserman identify the equality failure of their density-effect Wald interval. The inspected archival results do not determine the local expected-length objective with honesty over the full observational class. Kennedy's 2023 ACIC announcement already claims full-density minimax rates and localized fuzzy hypotheses; its exact theorem text remains externally unverifiable, so those achievements are not claimed as new.
fill: A coupled observable correction and a committed continuous observed-law family address the scalar length objective. The explicit rough-regime benchmark directs a test of every intermediate-radius term. Bias-aware triangular calibration remains a separate obligation before claiming an attaining interval.
